Updated the minds-evals improvement backlog (`specs/minds-eval-harbor/improvements.md`) now that per-trial cost and cache accounting is implemented.

The backlog had concluded that measuring eval spend required routing through the LiteLLM proxy, and therefore depended on the workspace credential change. It does not: the workspace event stream already carries a per-message token breakdown, so the driver's own transcript is a complete record. The section now records what was built, why the transcript source also covers timed-out trials and prices already-captured ones, and what LiteLLM is still worth wiring up for later (authoritative billed cost, non-claude harnesses, and a cross-check).

Records the decision to run a LiteLLM proxy inside the eval box: what a proxy buys that the transcript cannot (an unevadable metering boundary, deeper cache data, and a place to tighten the box's egress), why in-box rather than a deployed instance (Modal stays the only infrastructure dependency, and it leaves a seam for a model-swapping router behind it), and that it is credentialed by the same `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` the eval already uses rather than the product's customer-billing key-issuance path. Also records what delegation actually looks like when measured -- worker agents launched by the workspace's own turn-end hardening flow, not subagent tool calls.

Adds a fast-mode section to the backlog. Minds runs its chat agent in fast mode by default and fast mode bills the same tokens at twice the standard rate, which is now priced correctly wherever the tier is observable (the proxy) and reported as a floor where it is not. What remains recorded there: that mngr's own usage reporting has the same gap in production and nothing outside a proxy can see the tier, that fast mode is Opus-only so a per-model comparison leaving it at its default is not comparing like with like, and that pinning the tier per arm belongs with the model-override work.
